sources.title: Local gradient and negative-log loss meaning
sources.details: For a single correct class probability p, L=-ln(p); dL/dp=-1/p<0 for0<p<=1, so lower p means larger penalty. Across the same nonignored targets, the default code averages these losses; experts=0 makes its extra routing term zero. For differentiable L(theta), a sufficiently small delta gives L(theta+delta)≈L(theta)+sum_i (dL/dtheta_i)delta_i; the gradient is local sensitivity, and ||gradient||2 is only signal magnitude, not accuracy or guaranteed gain. No learning/generalization result follows from one finite nonzero gradient.
